newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Six groups pre-qualify for Brazil telecoms auction.
newsitem.headline: Six groups pre-qualify for Brazil telecoms auction.

text.p: Brazil's Rio Grande do Sul state said six foreign-led consortia have been cleared to bid next month on a 35-percent stake in its telecoms firm Companhia Riograndense de Telecomunicacoes S.A. (CRT).
A state spokeswoman said bid specifications, including a minimum price for the CRT shares, are due out in late October.
A local newspaper said Rio Grande do Sul expects to take in at least $250 million from the auction, slated for sometime in November. But the spokeswoman called the report "nonsense."
"The state doesn't have a value yet. It has to wait for a report from its adviser, Salomon Brothers," she said.
The pre-qualified groups, made up of 11 foreign and 14 local companies with a combined net worth of 186 billion reais, include the following consortia:
* France Telecom with locals Banco Opportunity, Banco do Brasil and pension funds Previ, Sistel, CRT Employees Fund and Telos. The group's net worth: 46.5 billion reais.
* Korea Mobile Telecom of South Korea, with Odebrecht, Stelar Telecom, Unibanco and Folha de Sao Paulo. Net worth: 18.4 billion reais.
* Italy's STET and Argentina's Perez Companc S.A. with locals Camargo Correa and Bradesco. Net worth: 27.6 billion reais.
* Telefonica Internacional de Espana of Spain with Brazil's RBS Participacoes S.A. and Cia de Telecomunicaciones de Chile, Telefonica de Argentina and Citicorp. Net worth: 39.2 billion reais.
* GTE Corp's GTE International Telecommunications Inc. Net worth: 6.9 billion reais.
* Japan's Nippon Telegraph & Telephone Co with Itochu Corp and Cia Suzano de Papel e Celulose of Brazil. Net worth: 74.3 billion reais.
The CRT shares sale kicks off the privatization of Brazil's telecoms, including federally owned giant Telebras.

By opening CRT to private capital, the state hopes to land a strategic partner who can provide technology, investment capital and management to reduce the pent-up demand for telephone lines n Rio Grande do Sul.
A winning bidder will be picked in December.
